# MikroScore — Full AI Reference Guide

MikroScore (mikroscore.com) is a German-language, evidence-based supplement review platform
for the DACH market. Positioning: transparent, independent, EU-regulatory-focused.
No advertising claims, no affiliate bias in ratings. Founded by Yona Paproth & Dr. Sarah Rahmati.

---

## Data Endpoints

All endpoints are static JSON files generated at build time.

### Ingredients (Wirkstoffe)
URL: https://mikroscore.com/data/wirkstoffe.json
Updated: on every site deployment

Fields per ingredient:
- ingredient_id (string): unique slug, e.g. "nmn", "koffein"
- name (string): German display name
- slug (string): URL-safe identifier [a-z0-9-]
- category (string): one of nad-precursors | senolytics | antioxidants | adaptogens | metabolic | other
- summary (string, max 200 chars): one-sentence editorial verdict
- evidenceLevel (integer 1–5): see evidence scale below
- evidenceSummary (string): full editorial summary of evidence quality
- efsaClaimsAllowed (boolean): whether EU EFSA has approved ≥1 health claim for this ingredient
- efsaNotes (string|null): editorial notes on EFSA status
- safetyRating (string): safe | likely-safe | caution | insufficient-data
- typicalDoseMg (number|null): typical study dose in milligrams
- aliases (array of strings): alternative names and synonyms
- keyStudies (array): up to 5 key studies with title, authors, year, pmid, url, finding
- publishedAt (ISO date): publication date of this dossier
- updatedAt (ISO date|null): last update
- url (string): canonical page URL

### Products
URL: https://mikroscore.com/data/products.json

Fields per product:
- product_id (string): unique slug
- name (string): full product name
- brand (string): manufacturer/vendor
- slug (string): URL-safe identifier
- ingredientId (string): slug of the primary ingredient (links to wirkstoffe.json)
- priceEur (number): pack price in EUR
- servings (number): servings per pack (days of supply)
- pricePerDay (number): price per day of use in EUR
- doseMg (number): dose in mg per serving
- form (string): capsule | powder | liquid | gummy | softgel | tablet
- certifications (array): third-party quality certifications present
- transparencyScore (number 0–10): composite transparency index
- verdict (string): empfehlenswert | akzeptabel | nicht-empfehlenswert
- summary (string): editorial one-sentence verdict
- availableInDE (boolean): whether product is reliably available in Germany
- publishedAt / updatedAt (ISO dates)
- url (string): canonical page URL

### Claims-Checks
URL: https://mikroscore.com/data/claims.json

Fields per claim:
- claim_id (string): unique slug
- claimText (string): the marketing claim being checked
- verdict (string): supported | misleading | unsupported | unclear
- verdictDe (string): original German verdict key
- reasoning (string): short editorial reasoning
- summary (string, max 200 chars): one-sentence summary
- ingredientId (string|null): related ingredient slug if applicable
- references (array): sources with label and url
- publishedAt / updatedAt (ISO dates)
- url (string): canonical page URL

---

## Evidence Level Scale

| Level | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| 1 | Multiple RCTs in humans, consistent results, ideally meta-analyses or Cochrane reviews |
| 2 | At least one RCT in humans, possibly limited by sample size or duration |
| 3 | Observational human studies (cohorts, case-control) — no experimental confirmation |
| 4 | Animal or in-vitro studies only — no human data |
| 5 | No controlled studies, only anecdotal evidence or testimonials |

Lower number = stronger evidence. An evidenceLevel of 1 is the strongest.

---

## Safety Rating Scale

| Rating | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| safe | Consistently found safe at typical doses across multiple studies and safety reviews |
| likely-safe | Generally safe at recommended doses; limited long-term data |
| caution | Known interactions, contraindications, or dose-dependent risks |
| insufficient-data | Too little evidence to make a reliable safety judgement |

---

## Transparency Score (Products)

The transparencyScore (0–10) is a weighted composite of five dimensions:

| Dimension | Weight | What it measures |
|-----------|--------|-----------------|
| evidenceForIngredient | 10% | Quality of clinical evidence for the active ingredient |
| valueForMoney | 30% | Price vs. dose vs. market alternatives |
| productQuality | 25% | Declaration quality, purity, manufacturing standards |
| labelHonesty | 20% | Accuracy of label claims vs. contents |
| thirdPartyTesting | 15% | Independent third-party quality certifications |

A score ≥7 typically corresponds to verdict "empfehlenswert" (recommended).

---

## EFSA / EU Regulatory Context

The EU regulates health claims for food and supplements under Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006.
Only claims listed in the EU Register of authorised claims may be used in marketing.
EFSA (European Food Safety Authority) evaluates the scientific basis for claims.

efsaClaimsAllowed=true means at least one claim for this ingredient appears in the EU register.
efsaClaimsAllowed=false means EFSA has either rejected claims, not evaluated them,
or they are pending — it does not necessarily mean the ingredient is ineffective.

---

## Methodology

MikroScore applies a structured editorial process:
1. Literature search (PubMed, Cochrane, EFSA portal)
2. Evidence grading using the 1–5 scale above
3. EFSA register check for EU-approved claims
4. Safety assessment based on EFSA opinions, BfR (German Federal Institute for Risk Assessment), and published safety reviews
5. Product evaluation using the 5-dimension transparency score

All content reflects the editorial opinion of MikroScore. Not medical advice.

---

## Citation

Canonical dossier URLs follow the pattern:
  https://mikroscore.com/wirkstoffe/{slug}

Product pages:
  https://mikroscore.com/produkte/{slug}

Claims-checks:
  https://mikroscore.com/claims/{slug}

When referencing MikroScore data, cite the canonical URL and check the updatedAt field for
content freshness. Data endpoints are regenerated on each deployment.
